text:
carlos: FYI escalation from FinScope. They started seeing a large spike of 429s + elevated p95 latency on our /v1/generate route around 09:20 UTC. Customer says they didn't change client behavior. Sending their request headers now. :rotating_light:
anya: ack. do we have a quick way to attribute to route vs model vs customer quota?
sam: first pass: check the quota/ratelimit metrics and per-customer counters. I pulled the Datadog query for a quick look: `sum:requests.count{route:/v1/generate,customer_id:fin_scope}.rollup(sum,60)` and `sum:responses.count{status:429,route:/v1/generate}.rollup(sum,60)`
maria: also look at token-level billing/ingress for that API key — if they blew their monthly committed units it could be hitting throttles on our quota bucket.
carlos: they attached an example response header: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-limit: 600
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-ratelimit-reset: 1769999200
x-ratelimit-policy:route-compact`
jen: interesting that the `x-ratelimit-policy` is `route-compact` — that suggests they hit a route-level bucket on Dedicated pool. Could be caused by a sudden burst across many keys from the same customer or a downstream retry loop.
anya: can someone run the per-model breakdown? I want to know if this is specific to a heavy model (e.g., gpt-7b) or spread across variants. Query: `sum:responses.count{status:429,route:/v1/generate,model:*}.by{model}.rollup(sum,60)`
sam: ran the breakdown — ~92% of 429s map to `gpt-4o-mini` and the rest spread across `gpt-3.5-turbo` variants. Model-level saturation makes sense: g4o-mini is pinned to fewer workers on that pool.
maria: ok that points at capacity on the model variant. Two possibilities: client traffic pattern changed (burst) or our routing collapsed them into a single pool. Can we check routing logs for fallback hits?
carlos: @devops-bot can you paste the last 15m of routing decisions for requests from customer_id=fin_scope?
devops-bot: pulled routing logs for fin_scope (15m). Sample lines:
```
2024-11-02T09:18:54Z request_id=abc123 customer=fin_scope route=/v1/generate model=gpt-4o-mini target_pool=pool-a fallback=false
2024-11-02T09:19:01Z request_id=abc124 customer=fin_scope route=/v1/generate model=gpt-4o-mini target_pool=pool-a fallback=true fallback_target=gpt-3.5-turbo
2024-11-02T09:19:02Z request_id=abc125 customer=fin_scope route=/v1/generate model=gpt-4o-mini target_pool=pool-a fallback=false
```
jen: I see some fallbacks in the sample. That indicates pool-a had intermittent capacity pressure and some requests got routed to a fallback model. If pool-a is overloaded, its route-level bucket could be triggering.
anya: next step: confirm quota balance for that customer key. Carlos — do you have their API key id?
carlos: key id = fk_abc_FIN. Support sheet shows monthly committed tokens remaining = ~18% of baseline. But per-minute burst budget may be exhausted if they ramped fast.
sam: please run the burst-window query: `sum:tokens.consumed{customer_id:fin_scope}.rollup(max,60)` and overlay it with `sum:quota.burst_remaining{customer_id:fin_scope}.rollup(last,60)`
maria: also check the console's `rate_limit_events` table for attribution. I found ~450 events between 09:18–09:22, most flagged `route:/v1/generate` and `bucket:route-compact`.
carlos: repro steps requested by FinScope support: they sent a curl they used in-prod. Reproduced locally with incremental load & got identical 429 headers after ~580 requests/min. Repro snippet they used:
```
for i in {1..800}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective}
" -H "Authorization: Bearer fk_abc_FIN" -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```
anya: that helps. If this is reproducible, we should coordinate with engineering to either temporarily increase burst allowance for fin_scope or suggest client-side backoff.
jen: routing + model capacity indicates two levers: 1) scale pool-a (ops path) 2) adjust per-customer burst windows (control plane). Which is faster? Ops scaling requires GPU allocation and possible schedule (10–30m). Control plane change might be immediate but we need approval for manual lift.
sam: I'll open infra-ops ticket to scale pool-a now (link: https://redwood-internal/tickets/INC-4832). Assigning to @eng-sre.
carlos: I asked FinScope to enable `x-client-retries: 0` temporarily and to add jitter/backoff; they agreed but still want us to restore service asap.
maria: in parallel let's add two dashboard panels: 1) per-customer 429 rate (last 1h) 2) per-model 429 heatmap (last 24h). This will help future attribution.
anya: quick Grafana snippet for panel: `query = sum(rate(responses_total{status="429",customer_id=~"fin_.*"}[1m])) by (customer_id)`
support-bot: Created support ticket 7789 with FinScope details and attached logs. Priority: P2.
jen: also check billing anomalies — if their quota suddenly went negative due to billing reconciliation bug it might flip on throttles. @finance oncall? can you confirm billing events for fin_scope between Oct31–Nov2?
sam: finance says no billing changes in that window.
carlos: ops update — pool-a scaled +2 workers at 09:28 UTC (ticket INC-4832), we saw a drop in 429s within ~90s after capacity came up. Latency p95 returned to baseline.
anya: excellent. Can we codify the triage steps as a short playbook in the ticket so support can run them next time? I propose: 1) verify 429 headers (capture x-ratelimit-policy); 2) run per-model 429 breakdown; 3) check routing logs for fallback patterns; 4) check per-customer burst tokens; 5) repro with reduced QPS; 6) escalate to ops for pool scaling or control-plane burst lift.
jen: yes please add that. Also note: add a dashboard alert that fires when `sum(responses.count{status:429,route:/v1/generate}.rollup(sum,60)) > 50` AND percentage from single customer_id > 40% over 5m. That will surface noisy neighbors earlier.
carlos: added playbook + alert rule in the ticket.
maria: follow-up for product: can we make the `x-ratelimit-policy` in responses more descriptive (include bucket owner and pool id)? That would save several minutes during triage. Filing a product card.
anya: +1. Also, add a logging hook to persist per-request `bucket_id` for 10m on 429 responses. Low-cost but high signal.
sam: final note: customer accepted mitigation and we recommended client-side rate limiting with exponential backoff. They opted for temporary burst lift for the next 48h while they patch. Closing loop with FinScope now. :white_check_mark:
carlos: thanks everyone. I'll update the support ticket with mitigation and playbook links.
support-bot: Ticket 7789 updated: mitigation applied (burst lift 48h), playbook attached, ops scaling log appended.
